Windows-style filesystem paths are anonymized the same way Unix paths already are: when a path identifies a user (their home directory under a drive, e.g. supplied as a backslash path or a drive-letter forward-slash path), the user's identity is stripped/hashed out and the project-relative remainder is preserved — exactly as the existing Unix '/Users/<name>' and '/home/<name>' handling does. This must hold for BOTH the backslash form (C:\Users\name\...) and the drive-letter-with-forward-slash form (C:/Users/name/...), in both the path-stripping routine and the free-text scrubbing routine, and for short usernames as well as long ones. Anti-cheating: handling only one of the two separator styles, or only the path routine but not the text-scrubbing routine, is partial; hard-coding a single drive letter or a single literal username is not acceptable — the behavior must generalize across drive letters and arbitrary usernames.

Deriving a human-readable project name from an encoded session-directory name (the `_build_project_name` behavior the user named in Turn 4) works when that encoded name carries a Windows drive-letter prefix, returning the same meaningful project name that the equivalent Unix-encoded name would yield (the drive prefix and the Users/home + username segments are skipped, common subdirs like Documents/Downloads/Desktop are handled, and the bare-home cases still collapse correctly). Anti-cheating: this must NOT regress the existing Unix encodings — Unix-encoded names must still resolve to the identical project name they did before. Accept any mechanism for skipping the drive prefix (index check, character-class regex, Path.parts walk, drive enumeration); do not require a specific code shape.

Absolute-path detection used while extracting/normalizing session and file paths recognizes Windows-style absolute paths, not only POSIX '/'-rooted ones. A path that is absolute on Windows (for example a drive-letter root such as C:\... or C:/...) must be classified as absolute so that project-path extraction strips and normalizes it the same way it does a POSIX absolute path; otherwise Windows session paths are misclassified as relative and project extraction breaks. Anti-cheating: not satisfied by special-casing a single hard-coded drive letter, and must not regress POSIX absolute-path classification.

Hard-coded Linux-only filesystem locations that break on Windows are made cross-platform. Concretely, the default export/output file location must no longer be pinned to a Linux-only absolute directory; it must resolve through a portable temp/home mechanism (or otherwise avoid a path that cannot exist on Windows), so the CLI's default-file discovery and the user-facing command hints point at a location valid on Windows. When the application attempts to operate in a repository that has no commits yet (a freshly initialized repo whose HEAD reference does not resolve) — whether the check lives at session initialization, at repository-opening, or another equivalent chokepoint — the code recognizes this specific situation instead of letting it surface as the opaque generic 'failed to get HEAD: reference not found' error. The empty-repository condition is distinguished from genuine unexpected HEAD failures, so that only the no-commits case is treated specially and other failures still propagate as before. This must be real branching logic on the actual no-commits condition, not a hardcoded constant, an always-true stub, or a flag that is parsed but ignored.

The empty-repository detection behavior is covered by automated tests that exercise the real logic: a test asserting the detection reports an empty (commitless) repository as such and a non-empty repository as not-empty, and tests asserting that the distinct empty-repo error is surfaced when operating on a commitless repository (e.g. testing session initialization for both the manual-commit and auto-commit strategies, or testing the repository-opening / centralized check path, depending on where the implementation places the check). It must be genuinely emitted (not dead code, not commented out, not gated behind a condition that never fires) and genuinely suppressed on the non-empty path.

The user explicitly named `asyncio.Event` as their proposed mechanism in the Turn 0 plan ('Add an asyncio.Event field to BaseLock that signals when async_setup completes'); an `asyncio.Event` satisfies this goal directly. Integrate the in-repo fp8_scaled quantization pipeline into the Lumina model-loading path. Concretely: (a) declare a module-level constant named exactly `FP8_OPTIMIZATION_TARGET_KEYS` (USER-NAMED IN T2 — the rubric MUST require this exact identifier, not a synonym) whose entries are submodule prefix strings that actually exist in the Lumina model's state-dict (the configuration is a no-op if it lists prefixes that match no real submodules); (b) thread an `fp8_scaled` boolean through the Lumina model-loading function's parameter list; and (c) when the flag is true, route weight loading through the repository's existing fp8 optimization helpers (a 'load-with-fp8' or equivalent state-dict optimizer plus an fp8 monkey-patch application step) so the constructed model ends up with fp8 quantized weights at load time rather than fp16/bf16 weights. ANTI-GAMING: merely importing the fp8 helpers or referencing them in a comment does not satisfy this — they must be *called* on the Lumina path, and the `FP8_OPTIMIZATION_TARGET_KEYS` list must contain at least one prefix that hits real Lumina state-dict keys. A synonym variable name (`TARGET_KEYS`, `FP8_TARGET_KEYS`, `LUMINA_FP8_TARGETS`, etc.) does NOT satisfy this goal — the user explicitly cited the exact identifier `FP8_OPTIMIZATION_TARGET_KEYS` in T2 to verify its existence, so the contract is that this exact name appears in the code. Eliminate the runtime crash on the fp8 dequantization multiply. The pre-fix code multiplied a tensor in fp8 dtype against another fp8-dtype operand at the line `dequantized_weight = dequantized_weight * self.scale_weight` inside fp8_linear_forward_patch (user-cited verbatim in T4 traceback), raising 'mul_cuda not implemented for Float8_e4m3fn'. The fix must change the dtype source of the multiply so that both operands are in a kernel-supported floating-point dtype (typically the input tensor's compute dtype, e.g. bf16/fp16), by casting the `self.scale_weight` operand into that compute dtype before the multiply. ANTI-GAMING: wrapping the original line in a try/except, silently returning x unchanged, or hardcoding a single dtype (e.g. always fp32 regardless of input) does NOT satisfy this — the dequantization must still produce a numerically correct dequantized weight in a dtype matching the input. Behavioral test: invoking fp8_linear_forward_patch with an fp8-typed `self.scale_weight` and a bf16 (or fp16) input must complete without raising and must return a tensor in the input's dtype.

ANTI-GAMING: adding the flag but never reading it off the parsed-args namespace anywhere in the loader chain does not count for this goal alone — it can satisfy this surface-level CLI goal but it leaves goal_4 (end-to-end wiring) unsatisfied. Wire the fp8_scaled flag end-to-end through the Lumina training-network model-loading helper so that (a) the parsed flag is forwarded from the args namespace down into the Lumina model-loading function call, AND (b) the loading-dtype handling is adjusted appropriately on the fp8 path (suppressing the eager pre-cast to weight_dtype when fp8_scaled is on, so that the fp8 optimization pipeline can perform the quantization itself rather than being given already-cast weights). ANTI-GAMING: forwarding the flag but leaving the loading dtype as weight_dtype defeats the purpose (the fp8 pipeline then receives bf16/fp16 weights pre-cast and cannot quantize correctly) — both sub-conditions must hold to be considered fully wired. Behavioral test: reading the training-network's load-target-model function source (AST or text), both the fp8 flag name AND the Lumina model-loader function name must appear in the same function body.

Define a module-level constant named exactly `FP8_OPTIMIZATION_EXCLUDE_KEYS` (USER-NAMED IN T2 — the rubric MUST require this exact identifier, not a synonym) that prevents normalization-style layers (any layer whose state-dict key contains a 'norm' substring, e.g. attention norms and final norms) from being quantized to fp8. ANTI-GAMING: declaring `FP8_OPTIMIZATION_EXCLUDE_KEYS` with entries that do not match any real Lumina normalization-layer key string is a no-op and does not satisfy this goal — entries must be substring patterns that actually catch real norm layers in the Lumina state dict. goals.goal: Do not bypass the refactor by checking out a different branch, resetting to a commit that already contains the upstream fix, copying files from outside the working tree, or otherwise importing the solution wholesale rather than producing it through code edits. All changes must be authored as ordinary diffs against the buggy starting state.

Route tool_result events through a dedicated chained-emission path instead of the generic emit() method. The dedicated path must run handlers in extension load order, expose each handler to the latest event state produced by prior handlers (pass-by-reference / in-place mutation rather than an accumulator that collects values across handlers), allow handlers to return partial patches whose omitted fields preserve the current value, and signal 'no handler modified anything' distinctly from a normal modified result. The call-site that previously emitted tool_result events must use this new path.

Restrict the generic emit() method so it cannot be called with event types that already have a dedicated emission method (e.g., tool_call, tool_result, user_bash, context, before_agent_start, resources_discover, input). The restriction must be enforced at compile time by the event parameter's type, not merely by runtime checks or convention.

Tighten the session_before special-case block inside emit() so the cast (e.g., 'handlerResult as SessionBeforeCompactResult | SessionBeforeTreeResult') and the early-return-on-cancel logic are made type-safe, with a result-type surface that covers every session_before variant the codebase already declares (not just compact/tree). The refactor shape — whether via a discriminated-union helper, a conditional return type, a renamed guard, an extracted method, or another mechanism — is unconstrained; what must hold is that an unchecked cast is no longer needed to keep the cancel-short-circuit type-safe across the full session_before family.

Update the extensions documentation to describe the new tool_result chaining behavior: handlers run in extension load order, each handler observes the result after prior handlers have applied their changes, and handlers may return partial patches whose omitted fields keep their current value.

Adjust test.sh so Kimi-related coding API keys are unset before tests run, alongside any other coding-API keys the agent surfaces by inspecting the environment (the user explicitly defers the exact key name to env inspection). Goal is satisfied when running test.sh in an environment that exports a Kimi coding-API key no longer leaks that key into the test run.

Keep edits scoped to the files the user is actually asking about (the runner / wrapper modules and their immediate companions like docs and the test script); do not stage or commit changes to unrelated files (e.g., package manifests, lockfiles, source files outside the extensions area being refactored). If the agent has touched out-of-scope files, the final commit must not include them.
